cards.text: Book of Judges, friend: "Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD." AGAIN, like me hitting snooze for the fifth time and acting shocked I'm late. So the LORD delivers them into an enemy's hand.

cards.question: Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD again. Who does He deliver them into the hand of?
Israel stays in the hand of the Philistines for ___ years.

cards.text: Now meet Manoah, a man from Zorah, from the clan of the Danites. His wife was barren and had no children, and that's right where this story starts.
Then the angel of the LORD shows up. Not to Manoah. To his wife.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah's wife it is true she is barren. Then what does he tell her?

answers.text: She will give birth to a son
She will give birth to twins
She will give birth to a daughter

cards.text: And he's not done. "Now please be careful," he says, and he gives her things to stay away from, starting right now.

cards.question: The angel tells Manoah's wife not to drink wine or strong drink, and not to eat anything ___.

cards.text: Then the angel gets specific about the boy: "no razor shall touch his head." A lifetime of no haircuts, friend. My mustache is jealous.

cards.question: No razor will touch the boy's head. What does the angel say the boy will be to God from the womb?
The angel says the boy will finish the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.

cards.text: So the woman goes and tells her husband a man of God came to her. She says his appearance was like the angel of God, "exceedingly awesome."

cards.question: Manoah's wife tells him she asked the man of God where he came from.
Manoah's wife repeats the message to him. How long does she say the boy will be a Nazirite to God?

answers.text: From the womb until his death
From the womb until he is grown
From his birth until he marries

cards.text: Manoah takes it all in. No panicking, no group chat, he goes straight to the LORD in prayer.

cards.question: Manoah prays to the LORD about the man of God. What does he ask for?

answers.text: That the man would come again to teach them
That the LORD would give them a sign first
That the boy would be born very soon

cards.text: "And God listened to the voice of Manoah." The angel of God comes back to the woman while she's sitting in the field.

cards.question: When the angel of God returns, Manoah is in the field with his wife.

cards.text: She runs quickly to tell her husband the man is back. Manoah prays for a second visit and misses it, like waiting all day on a delivery, stepping away for ONE minute, and coming back to a sticky note.
So Manoah got up and followed his wife. He walks right up and asks, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?"

cards.question: The man tells Manoah he is the one who spoke to his wife.

cards.text: Then Manoah asks, "When your words come to pass, what will be the boy’s rule of life and mission?" I spent years next to a pile of instruction manuals, friend, and Manoah would've read EVERY one.

cards.question: Manoah asks about the boy's rule of life and mission. How does the angel of the LORD answer?

answers.text: His wife must do all the angel told her
Manoah must take the boy to the priests
Manoah must teach the boy to fight

cards.question: The angel adds that Manoah's wife must not eat anything that comes from the vine.

cards.text: Manoah begs him to stay so they can prepare a young goat for him. This man is NOT letting a guest leave without feeding him.

cards.question: Manoah offers to prepare a young goat for the angel of the LORD. What does the angel say?

answers.text: He won't eat but they may offer it to the LORD
He will stay and eat it with them gladly
They should save it for the boy's birth

cards.text: Manoah still doesn't know it's the angel of the LORD. So he asks for a name, so they can honor him when his word comes to pass.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah his name.

cards.text: Instead he asks, "Why do you ask my name," and says it's beyond comprehension. So Manoah offers a young goat and a grain offering on a rock to the LORD, and as they look on, "the LORD did a marvelous thing."

cards.question: When the flame goes up from the altar to the sky, the angel of the LORD ___ in the flame.
When Manoah and his wife see the angel go up in the flame, they run from the altar.

cards.text: The angel of the LORD doesn't appear to them again, and "Manoah realized that it had been the angel of the LORD." Hey, I once asked an angel if he had the right drawer, so I'm not judging anybody.

cards.question: Manoah tells his wife they are going to ___, because they have seen God.
Manoah is sure they're going to die. What reason does his wife give that they won't?

answers.text: The angel promised them long life
They obeyed every rule he gave

cards.text: Manoah's panicking, and his wife walks in with receipts: He wouldn't have shown them all these things or spoken to them this way. Every panic needs one calm voice, friend, and it's usually not the guy yelling.
So the woman gives birth to a son and names him Samson, and somewhere a barber just sighed. "The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him."

cards.question: As Samson grows, something begins to stir him at Mahaneh-dan. What is it?

cards.text: Right there at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this boy's story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "no razor shall touch his head.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "A lifetime of no haircuts" tells the baker the boy's vow lasts his whole life. Card 14 then asks how long the boy will be a Nazirite, with the answer "From the womb until his death." Verse 5 also never says how long the vow lasts. That comes in verse 7.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card helps the baker reason out the forty years. It is a pure number guess, and it comes right after another discovery question on the same verse (card 2, the Philistines). The stop already has several other discovery picks (cards 10, 13 and 16).

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: "Manoah takes it all in. No panicking" states Manoah's inner state as fact. Verse 8 only says "Then Manoah prayed." "Goes straight" also adds a speed the text doesn't give. Later, stop 2 card 16 says Manoah is panicking.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The card says Manoah "misses" the second visit, and the joke ends with the visitor gone and only a sticky note left. In verse 11, Manoah follows his wife and talks with the man. He missed only the arrival, so the text shows that "misses it" and the visitor leaving are wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "Manoah begs him to stay" stretches verse 15. The text has a polite request: "Please stay here," Manoah said.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Manoah still doesn't know it's the angel of the LORD. So he asks for a name" makes not knowing the reason he asks. In verse 16, "For Manoah did not know" explains the exchange about the food. Verse 17 begins "Then," and the only reason it gives for asking is "so that we may honor you."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "So Manoah offers a young goat" makes the angel's refusal to give his name the reason for the offering. Verse 19 begins "Then Manoah took," which gives no reason.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This one story card has three moments: the angel's reply about his name, Manoah's offering on the rock, and the LORD doing a marvelous thing.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over copies the doc's example almost word for word: "And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend." It isn't a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
